instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine strainer under cold water, rubbing the grains, until the water runs clear. Leave it to drain. Halve the onion and slice it thin. Mince the garlic.
Heat a large, deep skillet or wide pot over medium heat. Add the pine nuts and stir for 2 minutes, until they're golden. Transfer them to a small bowl straight away.
Add the butter to the same pot. When it's melted, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and starting to brown.

Turn the heat to medium-high and add the beef with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Break it up with a spoon and cook for 6 minutes, until no pink is left and it has some brown edges. If there's more than a spoonful of fat in the pan, spoon it off.
Add the garlic, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg and pepper. Stir for 1 minute, until you can smell the spices.
Add the drained rice and stir for 1 minute, until every grain is coated.
Pour in 2 3/4 cups hot water and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Stir once, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom, and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 15 minutes. Don't lift the lid.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Scatter the pine nuts and parsley over the top. Serve hot.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Runs about 46 minutes, well over 30, so it's a weeknight dinner rather than a quick one: the rice needs 15 minutes covered plus a 5 minute rest after the meat is browned. The lead is Two Sleevers (4.79 from 41), written for a pressure cooker; I used its spices (allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg), pine nuts and beef, and cooked it on the stovetop. Every Little Crumb (5 from 9) and Mediterranean Twist (5 from 3) agree on browned spiced beef, basmati and toasted nuts; they differ on vermicelli, peas and raisins, which I left out, and on the water ratio, which runs from 1 to 1.5 up to 1 to 2. I used about 1 to 1.8 for a stovetop pot.
